chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Harun, from Mufazzal al-Madaini, from his father, from his grandfather, who said:

The Imam (peace be upon him) sent for me one day and seated me for lunch. When they brought the meal spread, there were no vegetables on it, so he restrained his hand. Then he said to the servant, 'Do you not know that I do not eat on a spread that has no greens? Bring me the greens.' The servant went and brought the vegetables and placed them on the spread. Then he (peace be upon him) extended his hand and ate.

key_terms.الْمَاضِي: The Imam (specifically Musa ibn Ja'far, the 7th Imam)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Madi do when vegetables were missing from his meal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of the Prophet's and Imams' dietary etiquette, specifically the emphasis on consuming vegetables (khubz/khudra) as a staple. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that such habits were not merely personal preferences but acts of worship and adherence to the Sunnah, promoting health and moderation. The incident underscores the importance of mindfulness in daily actions, even in mundane activities like eating.
